children: The Bank of England looks set to raise interest rates Thursday as expected, keeping sterling supported after recent gains, ING's Francesco Pesole says in a note. However, the bar for the BOE to surprise markets with strong signals about future tightening seems fairly high as another rate increase is fully priced in February, limiting sterling's potential to rise, he says. Sterling has little near-term potential to reverse lower versus the euro given French debt concerns. However, it faces less supportive short-term rate differentials versus the dollar as U.K. rate expectations are more sensitive to falls in oil prices, he says. The BOE decision is at 1200 GMT. The euro rises 0.1% to 0.8344 pounds. Sterling trades flat at $1.3475. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
